copy.blurb:
FIFA World Cup 2026 on Thursday, overnight UTC kickoff, brings South Africa and Korea Republic together. The Desk's read disagrees with the market on the Korea Republic side, by +15.1pp — and that disagreement is the Pick.

Elo numbers going in: South Africa 1620, Korea Republic 1770. That's a 150-point lead for Korea Republic — closer than a casual reader of the market price might assume. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: South Africa to win at 23%, the draw at 21%, and Korea Republic to win at 56%. Each number is a probability over the full range of plausible in-form, no-injury, ninety-minute scenarios — not a prediction of a scoreline.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: South Africa to win at 30%, the draw at 29%, and Korea Republic to win at 40%. Polymarket has Korea Republic at 40%, which prices out at American odds of +147; the model has the same side at 56%. The +15.1pp gap across them is the disagreement we're surfacing.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the Korea Republic side that lower bound is 47% — +6.7pp clear of the market's 40%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. Calibration tracks the closing market on the bulk sample; selection — picking the single side where the gap is wide — is where the engine's edge has to come from. This verdict is a selection call on the Korea Republic side.

The number above is the most recent read; it isn't frozen. With kickoff roughly 34 days out, the model is on the weekly refresh cadence; we'll move to daily once we cross the T-5d window. Injury news, the actual XI, and weather conditions at kickoff all feed back into the prior when they land. We republish on every refresh. The Desk surfaces edge; what to do with that surface is a reader's call.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Korea Republic a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +15.1pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: On every meaningful read, Korea Republic look stronger here than Polymarket has them. Model 56% vs market 40% — a +15.1pp gap on the favourite side.
copy.title: South Africa v Korea Republic · the model leans Korea Republic
